You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From cafb39600e7a73263122a0e2db052d691686378f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Bert Kenward <bkenward@solarflare.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2018 16:29:28 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] sfc: correctly initialise filter rwsem for farch

Fixes: fc7a6c287ff3 ("sfc: use a semaphore to lock farch filters too")
Suggested-by: Joseph Korty <joe.korty@concurrent-rt.com>
Signed-off-by: Bert Kenward <bkenward@solarflare.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
---
 drivers/net/ethernet/sfc/farch.c | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/sfc/farch.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/sfc/farch.c
index 8edf20967c82..e045a5d6b938 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/sfc/farch.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/sfc/farch.c
@@ -2794,6 +2794,7 @@ int efx_farch_filter_table_probe(struct efx_nic *efx)
 	if (!state)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 	efx->filter_state = state;
+	init_rwsem(&state->lock);
 
 	table = &state->table[EFX_FARCH_FILTER_TABLE_RX_IP];
 	table->id = EFX_FARCH_FILTER_TABLE_RX_IP;
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the lack of proper initialization of the read-write semaphore (`rwsem`) used to lock the filter for the farch (filter architecture) in the `efx_farch_filter_table_probe` function. This oversight could lead to race conditions or inconsistent states when accessing the filter table, as the semaphore was not set up before being used, potentially resulting in undefined behavior or crashes. The patch corrects this by adding the initialization of the semaphore with `init_rwsem(&state->lock);`.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the lack of proper initialization of the read-write semaphore (`rwsem`) used to lock the filter for the farch (filter architecture) in the `efx_farch_filter_table_probe` function. This oversight could lead to race conditions or inconsistent states when accessing the filter table, as the semaphore was not set up before being used, potentially resulting in undefined behavior or crashes. The patch corrects this by adding the initialization of the semaphore with `init_rwsem(&state->lock);`.
